claimed_technique: USERINFO-charset prefix leak (password contains char outside USERINFO allowlist)
verdict_summary: The regex prefix-leak mechanism is REAL on the sanitize-only code path, but every sink the researcher named is defeated downstream. The headline sink (remote_mirror.last_error) and the EE import path BOTH pass user:/password: so sanitize_unencoded does a literal Regexp.escape(password) replace and fully masks the secret. The only un-defeated path is CE-only (free self-managed) project_import_state#190 via ImportFailureService, and even there the leak is a partial prefix of a non-token password, shown only to a project admin viewing the project's own credential.

mechanism_confirmed.evidence: Gitlab::UrlSanitizer.sanitize("fatal: https://user:p\\a55w0rd@gitlab.com/x.git") => "fatal: https://user:p\\*****@gitlab.com/x.git" — URI_REGEXP matched only 'a55w0rd@gitlab.com'; everything left of the backslash ('user:p\\') survives unmasked.
mechanism_confirmed.leak_extent: Only the credential prefix up to the FIRST char outside USERINFO [\-_.!~*'()a-zA-Z\d;:&=+$,]/%hh. With backslash early in password, leak is 'user:p\\' (username + 1 char).

why_it_does_not_hold.reason: update_error_message passes user: user, password: password. sanitize_unencoded runs first: gsub(/Regexp.escape(user):Regexp.escape(password)@/, '*****:*****@'). Backslash is escaped literally so the real password matches and is fully masked. Verified: output 'https://*****:*****@gitlab.com'.

EE override of sanitized_failure_message passes user/password (from project.import_data). Same sanitize_unencoded full-mask. Covers gitlab.com and all EE self-managed (the EE module is prepended via ProjectImportState.prepend_mod_with).

reassignment_error= chains a SECOND sanitizer: ::Projects::ImportErrorFilter.filter_message after sanitize. ERROR_MESSAGE_FILTER=/[^\s]*/[^\s]*(?=(\s|\z))/ replaces any non-whitespace token containing '/' with [FILTERED]; every URL token contains '://' so the whole 'https://user:p\\*****@host...' becomes [FILTERED]. Verified.

import_service applies ImportErrorFilter.filter_message to e.message BEFORE it reaches the sanitizer, and renders project.safe_import_url (already masked) not raw creds. Whole URL token -> [FILTERED].
sanitized_message is computed but do_fail stores the RAW error_message; sanitized value is only used inside the rescue logger. The sanitizer is not the guard for the stored/rendered value here.
o11y logs the message (not a member-facing render); bulk_imports configuration.safe_url sanitizes the configured URL but bulk-import creds are tokens (within USERINFO charset) so fully masked.

preconditions: CE / free self-managed only (EE override at ee/project_import_state.rb:246 passes creds and fully masks)
exception.message must contain the cleartext credential (raw git/import error embeds full clone URL incl userinfo)

import/mirror password must contain a char OUTSIDE USERINFO allowlist (backslash, space, <, >, ^, |, {, }, double-quote, [, ], #, ?, /, @, or bare %). Standard PATs/tokens (ghp_, glpat-, oauth2, alphanumerics, _ - ! $ , ;) are ENTIRELY within USERINFO and get FULLY masked -> no leak. Verified.
no ImportErrorFilter in this specific chain (project_import_state#mark_as_failed lines 127-133 call sanitized_failure_message only)
only_residual_path.leaked_value: Partial prefix only: username + the password bytes up to the first non-USERINFO char (often just the username and 0-1 password chars).
only_residual_path.audience: Rendered via project import_error which is gated by :read_import_error / user_can_admin_project (api/entities/project.rb:110-111, _importing_alert.haml, detailed_import_status_type). Viewer is a project admin/maintainer viewing the project's OWN stored credential -> minimal real-world impact.

browser_execution: N/A (not XSS; last_error is html_escaped at views/projects/mirrors/_remote_mirror.html.haml:15 via html_escape).
reason: The USERINFO prefix-leak is real on the bare sanitize() path, but the named primary sinks (remote_mirror.last_error, EE import_state) pass user:/password: so sanitize_unencoded literal-escapes and fully masks the secret; the importer paths chain ImportErrorFilter which collapses the whole URL token to [FILTERED]. The single un-defeated path is CE-only, requires a non-token password with a special char, leaks only a short prefix, and surfaces only to a project admin viewing the project's own credential. The claimed broad credential disclosure does not reach a meaningful sink end-to-end.
